rawCodeComments.body:
### Promptless documentation updates

- [Update Theme sandbox restrictions for Twig collection filters](https://app.gopromptless.ai/suggestions/77050cfe-f4e2-4088-9f3c-ad82488bfcb9) updates the "Template sandbox restrictions" section of the 7.2 developer docs: the sandbox now blocks only risky functions, and Theme templates can use `map`, `filter`, `reduce`, `sort` and `find` with arrow-function callbacks. [Docs PR](https://github.com/mautic/developer-documentation-new/pull/714)
Can you please provide steps to test? What filter wasn't working?

Thanks for asking. The issue is the Mautic theme sandbox denylist, not a missing Twig filter.

### Reproduction

1. Use a clean Mautic 7.2.1 installation.
2. Create a theme under `themes/` with a `page.html.twig` template.
3. Add a normal collection-filter expression to the template:

```twig
{% block content %}
    {{ [3, 1, 2]|sort|join }}
{% endblock %}
```

4. Create a page using that theme and open its preview.

On the current 7.2.1 code, the sandbox policy rejects `sort` before Twig can execute it, because Mautic's `ThemeSandboxPolicy` contains a denylist for collection filters. The same applies to legitimate uses of `map`, `filter` and `reduce`.

### What the PR changes

The PR removes Mautic's redundant filter denylist. Twig's own sandbox still validates callable arguments, so ordinary collection-filter usage is allowed while PHP function-name callbacks remain blocked.

I tested the patched policy in a clean 7.2.1 Composer sandbox with these cases:

```twig
{{ [3, 1, 2]|sort|join }}
```

Result:

```
123
```

The RCE-style callback cases were also tested:

```twig
{{ ["id", 0]|sort("system")|join }}
{{ ["id", 0]|find("system") }}
```

Both are rejected by Twig's sandbox with a runtime security error. The existing `map`, `filter` and `reduce` callback regression tests remain in place, and the PR adds equivalent coverage for `sort` and `find`.

So the expected verification is:

- normal `sort`/collection-filter expressions render successfully;
- callbacks supplied as PHP function-name strings are rejected;
- no command output or file content is exposed.

The complete CI matrix for this PR is green, including PHPUnit, e2e, PHPStan, CS Fixer, Twig Lint and SonarCloud.

- Fixed a Translator cross-reference that pointed to a page that doesn't exist.

### Promptless documentation updates

- [Update ClassMetadataBuilder association-builder return types for Doctrine ORM 3](https://app.gopromptless.ai/suggestions/f4636ec1-6b9a-4bcc-a7ed-c9ef3578446c) corrects the documented return types for `ClassMetadataBuilder::createManyToMany()` and `createOneToMany()` to Doctrine's own builder classes, since this PR removes Mautic's decorator classes. [Docs PR](https://github.com/mautic/developer-documentation-new/pull/667)

> Also there is a lot of retyping to string which I don't understand.

DBAL 3 took mixed values. DBAL 4 changed `ExpressionBuilder` to accept only strings, so anything passed has to be a string now.

For example, see `ExpressionBuilder::eq()`

DBAL 3: https://github.com/doctrine/dbal/blob/77eb61f529ee8a99152afdc955ff606f7ce21474/src/Query/Expression/ExpressionBuilder.php#L115-L133
DBAL 4: https://github.com/doctrine/dbal/blob/205fdf552ffafe33c1d12a41a2d6c7217666c32c/src/Query/Expression/ExpressionBuilder.php#L66-L82

On `(string) ((int) $campaignId)` specifically:
```diff
-$q->expr()->eq('cl.campaign_id', (int) $campaignId),
+$q->expr()->eq('cl.campaign_id', (string) ((int) $campaignId)),
```

These values are embedded as SQL literals rather than bound parameters, so the `(int)` is the existing guard against injection, only the `(string)` is required by DBAL 4. I checked the cases where the parameter is already typed, they are all `?int` with no null guard, so dropping the `(int)` would turn null into `''` and emit `campaign_id = `.

You were right that much of it was noise, though 38 of the casts were on literals (`(string) (0)`, `(string) (1)`, `(string) (true)`, `(string) (200)`). Those are now plain `'0'`, `'1'`, `'200'`.

Binding these as parameters instead of embedding them would remove the remaining casts entirely, but that is a real refactor and it would be better to do it separately than in this PR.

For example
```diff
-    public function getCountsForPendingContacts($campaignId, array $pendingEvents, ContactLimiter $limiter): CountResult
+    public function getCountsForPendingContacts(int $campaignId, array $pendingEvents, ContactLimiter $limiter): CountResult
-                    $q->expr()->eq('cl.campaign_id', (string) ((int) $campaignId)),
+                    $q->expr()->eq('cl.campaign_id', (string) $campaignId),
```

Thanks @adiati98 — all three suggestions applied in the latest commit, and I dug into why the links weren't rendering.

- **Features list** → bare targets: `:ref:`html/email.html.twig``, `:ref:`html/form.html.twig``, `:ref:`html/page.html.twig``
- **Corresponding-file paragraph** → `:ref:`Twig files``
- **Form style-only Themes note** → `:doc:`/themes/forms``

**Root cause of the broken links:** `docs/conf.py` sets `autosectionlabel_prefix_document = True`, which generates document-prefixed labels (including the literal backticks in headings like `` ``html/email.html.twig`` ``). That's why neither the previous prefixed form nor a plain bare `:ref:` resolved. To make the bare-target syntax you requested actually work, I added explicit reference labels at the four target headings:

```
.. _Twig files:
.. _html/email.html.twig:
.. _html/page.html.twig:
.. _html/form.html.twig:
```

**Verification:** A full Sphinx build confirms all four cross-references now render as real internal links and `:doc:`/themes/forms`` resolves to "Customizing Forms". No new undefined-label or duplicate-label warnings. Vale passes on the edited lines (which sit inside the existing `.. vale off`/`.. vale on` block).

Heads-up: the bare `:ref:` format works only because of those added heading labels — without them, bare targets would still fail under this repo's `autosectionlabel_prefix_document` setting.

One architectural concern worth discussing is that this approach uses roles for two different concepts: the user’s access level and the user’s team/group boundary.

For example, if Italy marketers and Italy managers need different permissions, they cannot both simply use a `Italy` role. The installation may need roles like `Germany Marketer`, `Germany Manager`, `Italy Marketer`, `Italy Manager`, etc.

That can become harder to manage as the number of countries, offices, brands, or teams grows. It also makes cases like users belonging to multiple teams or managers needing cross-team access more difficult to model - this approach is not possible with permissions.

A separate team/group concept could keep these concerns apart: roles define what a user can do, while teams/groups define which records they can access.

Not saying this blocks the PR, but it feels worth discussing so we are clear whether same-role permissions are the right direction here.

@promptless-for-oss can you make a docs PR for this one please. We need one PR for user docs and one PR for the developer docs.

I was quite excited about the [proposal](https://community.mautic.org/processes/roadmap/f/4/proposals/200) as it was suggesting to bend Postgres with polyfills to support Mautic rather than bending Mautic to support Postgres. However, in this PR I can see major Mautic refactoring. Lots of ifs where one query is used for MySql and MariaDB and completely different query is used for Postgres. When you look at the size of this PR it's clear how massive change it is. It'll take weeks just to review this. I'm pretty sure there are tens of bugs hidden in this PR. So we'll need good user base that require Mautic running on Postgres that will help us review and test this PR. Because if it is still just 1% then such a massive change that makes the code even harder to maintain isn't worth it. This is why we've decided to drop support for Posgres in the first place.

I've considered a better database abstraction layer for Mautic for some time. Inserting another abstraction layer for all data-driven interactions is very appealing. Such a mechanism would allow us to use different backend data sources  depending on what's being requested. Have some documents in MongoDB? Go get them through the data layer Mongo datasource. Need to operate on your campaigns from Salesforce? Get them through the data layer's Salesforce datasource. This would prevent us from having to manage the seemingly neverending data sync issues that come hand-in-hand with our current integrations. 

There's plenty of architectural benefits of this approach. By managing the data layer in this way, we could intercept and act on any request for data, modifying or otherwise combining various data sources into a normalized structure. We could take a request like `$this->datalayer->contacts->all()` and pull in local db contacts, remote contacts from an API response, and query the filesystem of an old ERP. We could more easily implement an [event sourcing](https://eventsauce.io/) approach which comes with all sorts of benefits on its own (data rollbacks, replays, insight into what happened for audit purposes). 

That said, such a system could be rather impractical both to implement and in real world usage without major changes that go beyond the scope of what even this PR is trying to accomplish. I'm not opposed to supporting pgsql, but I would like to see it implemented in a particular way if we really want it. I'm open to discussion.

Thanks for the detailed reviews, @escopecz @shinde-rahul @dongilbert. You're right to call out the scattered DB-specific logic and the growth in scope.

The original plan was a small, contained change like the POC: mostly platform tweaks, quoting fixes, and minimal adjustments to keep everything working on both MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL without breaking existing installs. Doctrine 2.x limits cleaner abstraction options, so some conditionals and duplicated query parts crept in as we hit real edge cases in tests and production data. Things like LIKE vs ILIKE (with LOWER), REGEXP differences, date formatting (DATE_FORMAT vs TO_CHAR), GROUP BY strictness, and upsert behavior all needed handling. The PR ended up bigger than intended because covering those reliably took more work.

I won't promise a full cleanup in the next few days, but I will push the specific refactors you suggested: reduce the inline if ($isPostgres) branches where possible, centralize more of the dialect-specific building (following @shinde-rahul's idea of a clearer abstraction point), and clean up the duplicated methods.

All scattered platform checks and all shared code handling the differences between the PostgreSQL and MySQL dialects will be implemented in the DatabasePlatform class (single place to review), which looks like the best place for this purpose. This will eliminate the need for scattered If(platform) checks throughout the core code.

These reviews were actually expected and were exactly the reason this PR was being a draft. To get the working code reviewed early and gather feedback on the approach. The code itself works, but the current implementation is not yet at the production standard. That's why I wanted reviews before finalizing the architecture.

On maintenance: as mentioned before, I will personally handle PostgreSQL-related fixes going forward. I'm already running this fork in production (sending ~10 million emails/month), so any conflict, bug, or incompatibility that surfaces gets fixed on my side. No extra burden on the core team.

So the current plan is to:
- Short term (coming weeks): address the review comments, reduce scattering, improve query handling for the mentioned differences.
- After that: keep the PR focused on compatibility without major refactoring.
- Ongoing: I maintain Postgres fixes; core stays MySQL-first.

@escopecz Update (following @shinde-rahul's idea of a clearer abstraction point):

Consolidated platform-specific logic into the central **Mautic\CoreBundle\Doctrine\DatabasePlatform** class.
Remaining **DatabasePlatform::isPostgreSQL()** checks and why they stay:
1. **app/bundles/InstallBundle/EventListener/DoctrineEventSubscriber.php** → **postgreSqlMySqlCompact()** method - runs only on PostgreSQL during schema generation to create MySQL compatibility functions/operators (e.g. **date_format**, **convert_tz**, **ifnull**, boolean/integer operators). This is intentional and required for fresh installs.
2. **app/bundles/InstallBundle/Helper/SchemaHelper.php** → **installSchema()**, **backupExistingSchema()**, **dropExistingSchema()** - handles PostgreSQL-specific differences during installation like dropping sequences, backing up/renaming sequences, skipping **foreign_key_checks** (which does not exist on PostgreSQL) etc. These paths are required for the installer to work correctly on both platforms.
3. **app/bundles/CoreBundle/Test/MauticMysqlTestCase.php** - several methods use platform checks for transaction/rollback behavior, sequence handling, psql vs mysql commands, and dump/reset SQL generation etc. These are test infrastructure and deliberately platform-aware.
4. Tests:
* app/bundles/LeadBundle/Tests/EventListener/CampaignSubscriberFunctionalTest.php (testRegexOperatorOnDateFieldCondition) - keeps $useCleanupRollback disabled only for MySQL (to avoid "There is no active transaction" exception occur on MySQL - original test creator intention).
* app/bundles/CoreBundle/Tests/Functional/EventListener/MigrationCommandSubscriberTest.php - generated columns assertions on PostgreSQL (they are not immutable in the same way, so the test is marked as partly skipped).
5. 7 legacy migration files - old migrations (not executed on new installs) but must still run successfully when importing/upgrading from very old databases. They contain checks for:
* **foreign_key_checks** (MySQL-only)
* table field types
* charset/collation handling (PostgreSQL uses different syntax/behavior here)

Everywhere else in the codebase, scattered inline **isPostgreSQL()** checks have been removed and replaced with calls to the centralized **DatabasePlatform** helpers.

The remaining checks are isolated to:
* installation schema preparation
* legacy migration compatibility
* test-specific edge cases

We've been running this branch (`7.x-postgresql`) against PostgreSQL 16 and hit a reproducible failure on every `doctrine:migrations:migrate` run:

```
SQLSTATE[42P16]: multiple primary keys for table "migrations" are not allowed
```

**Root cause**: `app/config/config.php` applies `PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES => true` to the connection options unconditionally (it's there as a MySQL/PHP 8.1 workaround). On `pdo_pgsql`, the option also stringifies the booleans returned by DBAL's schema-introspection queries against `pg_catalog` (e.g. `pg_index.indisprimary`/`indisunique`), which breaks DBAL's boolean handling — `introspectTable()` ends up reporting **zero indexes** for every table. doctrine-migrations then thinks the `migrations` table has no primary key and emits `ALTER TABLE migrations ADD PRIMARY KEY (version)` on every run → 42P16.

**Fix that works for us** — make the option conditional on the driver:

```php
'options' => 'pdo_pgsql' === $localConfigParameterBag->get('db_driver')
    ? []
    : [PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES => true],
```

With that change, introspection is correct and `mautic:install` + all migrations run cleanly on PostgreSQL; we have the branch passing our end-to-end suite (install → login → dashboard) with it.

> ```
> ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES
> ```

I've already removed the unconditional `PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES` (no longer needed with PHP 8.2+ / MySQL 8.4+).

## Pull request overview

Reintroduces PostgreSQL support across Mautic 7.x by adding a compatibility layer for DBAL/SQL differences (quoting, LIKE/ILIKE/regex, migrations, installer/config), while keeping MySQL/MariaDB behavior consistent.

**Changes:**
- Updates migrations and schema/index operations to be PostgreSQL-compatible and idempotent across platforms.
- Normalizes query behavior across DBs (identifier quoting, LIKE/ILIKE, regex, DISTINCT semantics, interval/time functions).
- Updates functional/unit tests and installer/config to run deterministically on PostgreSQL as well as MySQL/MariaDB.

rawCodeReviews.body: Works as expected 👍
Okay then
All set from my side.

I validated this locally,

### What I checked

1. Created a `Visits specific URL` point action in the UI.
2. Set:
   - Page URL: `https://example.com/pricing`
   - Total time spent: `60 seconds`
   - Returns after: `1 hour`
3. Saved the action successfully.
4. Confirmed the stored properties include:
   - `accumulative_time = 60`
   - `returns_after = 3600`

### Reproduction case

1. Contact has a previous hit for `https://example.com/pricing`.
2. That hit has `date_left` set so the dwell time is 90 seconds.
3. Only 10 minutes have passed.
4. The contact now visits `https://example.com/blog`.

### Actual result

`validateUrlHit()` returns `true`.

### Expected result

It should return `false`, because `returns_after = 3600` is configured but the current hit is not for `/pricing`, and only 10 minutes have passed.

The issue seems to be that `accumulative_time` is added to `$changePoints` from historical data, but `returns_after` is only added inside the `$urlMatches` block. When `$urlMatches` is false, the configured `returns_after` condition disappears from the final evaluation.

## Pull request overview Adds support for limiting `mautic:campaigns:summarize` to a single campaign via `--campaign-id`, ensuring both the “resume” cursor and summary updates are campaign-scoped. **Changes:** - Added `--campaign-id` option and campaign-specific console output for the summarize command. - Plumbed optional campaign ID through `SummaryModel` into the repositories’ “oldest triggered date” lookups and summary generation. - Added/updated automated test coverage for the campaign-limited summarization path. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 6 out of 6 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | app/bundles/CampaignBundle/Translations/en_US/messages.ini | Adds a new translated console message for campaign-scoped summarization output. | | app/bundles/CampaignBundle/Tests/Command/SummarizeCommandTest.php | Adds a test ensuring only the selected campaign receives summary rows when `--campaign-id` is provided. | | app/bundles/CampaignBundle/Model/SummaryModel.php | Threads optional campaign ID into oldest-date lookup and summarize execution. | | app/bundles/CampaignBundle/Entity/SummaryRepository.php | Adds optional campaign filtering to oldest summarized date lookup. | | app/bundles/CampaignBundle/Entity/LeadEventLogRepository.php | Adds optional campaign filtering to oldest event-log date lookup. | | app/bundles/CampaignBundle/Command/SummarizeCommand.php | Introduces `--campaign-id`, prints campaign-specific output, and passes campaign ID into the summarize flow. |

rawCodeReviews.body:
Code looks good. It works.

Maybe ... consider cache usage because of using COUNT() on big segments could be slow.
Can be added later in next PR.

TY!

Could you load these statistics asynchronously, similar to how you handle contact statistics with `contactStatsAction()` and `getStatsSummaryForContacts()`? Right now, these calls perform two full segment membership scans on every initial page load, including the filter-added count even when its card isn't displayed. This could become a performance issue on larger systems.

The new endpoint could return the total, manually added, and filter-added counts in a single aggregate query. You could then cache that result if segment membership changes can reliably invalidate it. Async loading or caching alone would still perform both scans on every cache miss.

Nice work on the combine optimization and the regression test for it.

Two things worth a look before merge, neither blocking:

1. `self::LIST_SEARCH_COMMAND` equals the literal string already used in the first two case labels (both are 'mautic.lead.lead.searchcommand.list'), so the last two case lines are dead duplicates. Probably leftover from introducing the constant. Removing them would also knock the switch back under Sonar's case-count limit.

2. collectSearchSegmentIdsByAlias doesn't check the `not` flag, so in theory `!segment:X source:manually_added` would still pull X into activeSegmentIds and check membership against a segment the query just excluded. Not tested, and the UI never generates that combination, so low risk, just flagging it.

## Pull request overview This PR adds Dynamic Web Content–style contact filters to Focus items so that eligible published Focus items can be automatically injected on tracked visits via `mtc.js`, without requiring manual embeds or campaigns. **Changes:** - Adds a nullable `filters` column to `focus` (via migration) and exposes it via serializer groups for Focus API read/write. - Extends the Focus edit UI with a new Filters tab using the existing DWC filters entry type/theme and shared filter JS initialization. - Implements automatic delivery: `mtc.js` conditionally calls a new public `/focus/check` endpoint which returns matching Focus item JS URLs for the tracked contact, with functional tests covering key scenarios. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 17 out of 17 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.

I've considered a better database abstraction layer for Mautic for some time. Inserting another abstraction layer for all data-driven interactions is very appealing. Such a mechanism would allow us to use different backend data sources  depending on what's being requested. Have some documents in MongoDB? Go get them through the data layer Mongo datasource. Need to operate on your campaigns from Salesforce? Get them through the data layer's Salesforce datasource. This would prevent us from having to manage the seemingly neverending data sync issues that come hand-in-hand with our current integrations. 

There's plenty of architectural benefits of this approach. By managing the data layer in this way, we could intercept and act on any request for data, modifying or otherwise combining various data sources into a normalized structure. We could take a request like `$this->datalayer->contacts->all()` and pull in local db contacts, remote contacts from an API response, and query the filesystem of an old ERP. We could more easily implement an [event sourcing](https://eventsauce.io/) approach which comes with all sorts of benefits on its own (data rollbacks, replays, insight into what happened for audit purposes). 

That said, such a system could be rather impractical both to implement and in real world usage without major changes that go beyond the scope of what even this PR is trying to accomplish. I'm not opposed to supporting pgsql, but I would like to see it implemented in a particular way if we really want it. I'm open to discussion.

We've been running this branch (`7.x-postgresql`) against PostgreSQL 16 and hit a reproducible failure on every `doctrine:migrations:migrate` run:

```
SQLSTATE[42P16]: multiple primary keys for table "migrations" are not allowed
```

**Root cause**: `app/config/config.php` applies `PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES => true` to the connection options unconditionally (it's there as a MySQL/PHP 8.1 workaround). On `pdo_pgsql`, the option also stringifies the booleans returned by DBAL's schema-introspection queries against `pg_catalog` (e.g. `pg_index.indisprimary`/`indisunique`), which breaks DBAL's boolean handling — `introspectTable()` ends up reporting **zero indexes** for every table. doctrine-migrations then thinks the `migrations` table has no primary key and emits `ALTER TABLE migrations ADD PRIMARY KEY (version)` on every run → 42P16.

**Fix that works for us** — make the option conditional on the driver:

```php
'options' => 'pdo_pgsql' === $localConfigParameterBag->get('db_driver')
    ? []
    : [PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES => true],
```

With that change, introspection is correct and `mautic:install` + all migrations run cleanly on PostgreSQL; we have the branch passing our end-to-end suite (install → login → dashboard) with it.

## Pull request overview

Reintroduces PostgreSQL support across Mautic 7.x by adding a compatibility layer for DBAL/SQL differences (quoting, LIKE/ILIKE/regex, migrations, installer/config), while keeping MySQL/MariaDB behavior consistent.

**Changes:**
- Updates migrations and schema/index operations to be PostgreSQL-compatible and idempotent across platforms.
- Normalizes query behavior across DBs (identifier quoting, LIKE/ILIKE, regex, DISTINCT semantics, interval/time functions).
- Updates functional/unit tests and installer/config to run deterministically on PostgreSQL as well as MySQL/MariaDB.

Verified Below scenarios, working as expected.
### 1. Email Preview Download Page Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | Admin can access download preview page | Navigate to `/email/download/preview/{emailId}` as admin | Page loads with top bar, contact/company lookups, iframe, and "Download HTML" button |
| 1.2 | Anonymous user blocked from unpublished email | Open `/email/download/preview/{emailId}` in incognito for unpublished email | HTTP 403 Forbidden |
| 1.3 | Anonymous user can access published email with public preview | Open `/email/download/preview/{emailId}` in incognito for published email with public preview enabled | Page loads successfully |
| 1.4 | Non-admin with viewown can access own emails | Login as non-admin with `email:emails:viewown`, access own email preview | Page loads successfully |
| 1.5 | Non-admin blocked from other users' emails | Login as non-admin with `email:emails:viewown`, try to access another user's email | HTTP 403 Forbidden |

### 2. Contact Token Rendering Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | Preview with contact shows real token values | Select a contact in the preview, email has `{contactfield=firstname}` | Contact's actual first name appears in preview |
| 2.2 | Preview without contact shows placeholder tokens | View preview without selecting contact | `[Firstname]` placeholder appears |
| 2.3 | Contact lookup updates preview dynamically | Change selected contact in lookup field | Preview iframe reloads with new contact's data |
| 2.4 | Clearing contact reverts to placeholders | Select contact, then clear the lookup field | Preview shows placeholder tokens again |

### 3. Company Token Rendering Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | Preview with company shows real token values | Select a company, email has `{companyfield=companyname}` | Company's actual name appears in preview |
| 3.2 | Preview without company shows placeholder tokens | View preview without selecting company | `[Companyname]` placeholder appears |
| 3.3 | Company lookup updates preview dynamically | Change selected company in lookup field | Preview iframe reloads with new company's data |
| 3.4 | Contact's primary company used when no company selected | Select contact with companies, don't select company manually | Contact's primary company tokens rendered |

### 4. Permission Enforcement Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | Non-admin cannot view contact they don't own | Login as non-admin with `viewown`, select contact owned by another user | Error flash: "You do not have access to this contact", tokens render as placeholders |
| 4.2 | Non-admin can view contact they own | Login as non-admin with `viewown`, select contact they own | Contact's real token values appear, no error |
| 4.3 | Admin can view any contact | Login as admin, select any contact | Contact's real token values appear |
| 4.4 | User with viewother can view any contact | Login with `lead:leads:viewother`, select any contact | Contact's real token values appear |

### 5. HTML Download Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1 | Download HTML without contact/company | Click "Download HTML" with no contact/company selected | File downloads as `email-name.html` with placeholder tokens |
| 5.2 | Download HTML with contact | Select contact "John", click "Download HTML" | File downloads as `john-email-name.html` |
| 5.3 | Download HTML with company | Select company "Acme Corp", click "Download HTML" | File downloads as `acme-corp-email-name.html` |
| 5.4 | Download HTML with both | Select contact and company, download | Company name takes precedence in filename |
| 5.5 | Downloaded HTML contains rendered tokens | Download with contact selected | HTML file contains actual contact data, not tokens |
| 5.6 | Special characters sanitized in filename | Contact name is "O'Neill", download | Filename is `o-neill-email-name.html` |

### 6. Company Lookup AJAX Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6.1 | Admin sees all companies | As admin, type in company lookup | All matching companies appear |
| 6.2 | Non-admin with viewown sees only owned companies | As non-admin with `viewown`, type in company lookup | Only companies they own appear |
| 6.3 | Company lookup returns correct format | Make AJAX call to `lead:companyList` | Returns `{id, value}` pairs with `success: 1` |

### 7. Draft Preview Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7.1 | Draft preview URL updates with contact/company | Select contact/company on email with draft | Draft preview URL includes `contactId` and `companyId` parameters |
| 7.2 | Draft preview shows draft content with tokens | Access draft preview with contact | Draft content displayed with contact's token values |
| 7.3 | Draft public preview requires published status | Access draft preview anonymously for unpublished email with public draft preview | Access denied |

### 8. Email Detail Page Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8.1 | Company lookup field visible | Open email detail page | Company lookup field appears alongside contact lookup |
| 8.2 | Preview URL updates with both IDs | Select contact and company | Preview URL contains both `contactId` and `companyId` params |
| 8.3 | Preview iframe updates on selection | Select contact or company | Iframe reloads with updated token values |
| 8.4 | Hidden input for company ID exists | Inspect page | `#content_preview_settings_company_id` hidden input present |

### 9. Token Regex Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9.1 | `{contactfield=X}` tokens matched | Email contains `{contactfield=email}` | Token is replaced |
| 9.2 | `{companyfield=X}` tokens matched | Email contains `{companyfield=companyname}` | Token is replaced |
| 9.3 | URL-encoded tokens matched | Email contains `%7Bcontactfield=email%7D` | Token is replaced |

### 10. Edge Cases & Security Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10.1 | Invalid email ID returns 404 | Access `/email/download/preview/99999` | HTTP 404 Not Found |
| 10.2 | Invalid contact ID ignored gracefully | Pass `contactId=99999` | Preview renders with placeholder tokens |
| 10.3 | Invalid company ID ignored gracefully | Pass `companyId=99999` | Preview renders with placeholder tokens |

Merge Risk

 **Merge Risk:** **🟡 Moderate** · up to `6d8cd` OpenID Connect login works in common setups, but several defects should be fixed before merging. Saving the configuration can silently remove every user's OpenID link. A provider error can trap users in a redirect loop. Some identity providers will fail registration because email and profile values are lost.

Security Architecture Review

 **Security architecture risk:** **🟠 High** · up to `6d8cd` The new registration flow can resolve an identity-provider username to an existing account and potentially inherit its privileges. Provider changes can also reuse old account associations, while unsuccessful configuration updates can erase them. These risks are conditional on configuration and provider behavior, but materially affect account ownership and authentication recovery. **Retained concerns** - **High · security · inferred:** New-account provisioning can silently become existing-account authentication. With registration enabled, an unused email and a preferred_username equal to a published target’s email can pass the factory’s separate email and username checks. The shared saveUser method then resolves that username against username OR email and returns the target account. If the target has no OIDC association, the attacker’s subject is linked to it and authentication inherits its role. This requires the provider to permit influence over the colliding claim; it does not require the target’s local credentials. The resolver predates the PR, but this OIDC caller introduces the exposure. - **High · security · inferred:** Durable associations are keyed only by the configured identity value, not by issuer. Changing the provider URL while retaining the mapping field preserves associations. A valid identity from the replacement issuer with the same subject value can therefore resolve to an account associated under the previous issuer. The single configured provider limits simultaneous exposure, but does not preserve the trust boundary across provider replacement; the mapping-field reset does not cover this transition. - **Medium · security · observed:** Changing the mapping field immediately deletes every persisted association in the form’s POST_SUBMIT handler. Connection validation and configuration-file writing happen later and can reject or fail the update. The old configuration can therefore remain active after its associations have been deleted, disrupting subsequent anonymous OIDC login and requiring account-link recovery. Configuration editing is administrator-only, which limits direct attacker authority but does not contain failed or interrupted configuration transitions. - **Low · security · observed:** The new credential factory sends selected identity-provider claims to debug logs and includes merged identity data in an error-level context when the identifier is missing. This introduces an additional destination for personal identity data beyond account persistence. Production error-level filtering limits routine debug exposure, but not the error path. This is the retained reportable privacy finding; the inspected contexts do not establish exposure of access tokens or client secrets.

Security review details

 **Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The registration-substitution path can reach published accounts without an existing OIDC association, including privileged accounts, when registration is enabled and the provider permits the required claim collision. Authentication loads the selected account’s permissions rather than restricting it to the configured registration role. The configuration-reset path affects all persisted associations in the application’s table. Broader tenant and deployment isolation were not established. **Security Findings and Attack Paths** - _inferred_ — A valid OIDC identity can cross into another local account through claim-driven registration and the shared username-or-email resolver, followed by durable subject linking and a self-validating authentication passport. Separately, a replacement issuer can reuse a previous issuer’s subject value. These are conditional source-to-account-authority paths, not demonstrated failures of token signature validation. - _observed_ — The retained privacy finding traces selected identity claims into logger contexts, including an error-level context on missing identifiers. Reading those logs requires access to the logging destination; the evidence does not show public log access or bearer-token disclosure. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — Local controls bind client construction to configured credentials and the current session, reject existing cross-user subject ownership, enforce registration enablement, and establish the new authentication passport after account selection. Issuer, audience, signature, nonce, state, and PKCE enforcement remain dependent on the unavailable external client implementation; their effectiveness was not verified by this review. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _inferred_ — Successful repeated callbacks reuse committed associations, and schema constraints contain duplicate ownership. Recovery is weaker across separate provisioning flushes and configuration/database transitions: partial failures can leave unlinked users or delete associations while retaining the old configuration. These intermediate states affect authentication availability and require recovery beyond simply repeating the failed operation. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — Separate OIDC account creation from implicit existing-account resolution. Reject identity collisions across both username and email namespaces, and require explicit authenticated ownership proof for any existing-account association. - _proposed_ — Persist issuer-scoped identity provenance and make provider or mapping changes explicit, recoverable transitions. Validate the complete configuration before destructive association changes, with an interruption-safe commit or reconciliation plan. - _proposed_ — Make user creation and association creation one recoverable unit, with explicit handling for uniqueness conflicts, interruption, and retries rather than leaving an unlinked account after a failed second write. - _proposed_ — Use an allowlist of non-personal diagnostic metadata instead of identity payloads in logs, and establish integration evidence for the exact external client’s callback and token-validation guarantees.

I've fixed the remaining Vale warnings, and `vale docs/components/dynamic_web_content.rst` now reports no alerts at any level.

All 13 were `Mautic.FeatureList` suggestions:

* Where "page" meant a general website page, it now says "website" or "detail view", so it doesn't read as a Mautic Landing Page.
* The **Published** field now uses the label the Dynamic Web Content form shows, **Available for use**.

The fix is in commit a78cc46 on this PR.

rawDocsComments.body: Thanks, @adiati98. I'm checking PR #1032 against the Mautic source and a running instance, including your note about describing what readers see on screen instead of explaining the label names, and I'll post my findings and a summary here without committing anything.

@adiati98, here's the review you asked for, with a summary first and then the details. Thanks to mahmudurrahmanlabib for the PR. I checked it (head `4bd1037`) against the `mautic/mautic` 7.2 source (`ce1679a`). I also ran Mautic 7.2 locally and tested scheduling on Campaigns whose dates I set directly in the database. Each test Campaign had one Contact and an action delayed by 10 days. Nothing was committed or pushed, and no PR was opened.

**Summary:** Most of the content is accurate. Five items need fixing:
- Rewording line 60, per your comment.
- A too-narrow statement about where the activation message appears.
- A change in quote style.
- An ambiguous example label.
- An inconsistent option label.

Three details are missing: scheduled activation, what the details panel shows, and, optionally, manual reschedule or cancel.

### Confirmed accurate
- The labels match the UI:
  - The **Campaign Republish Behaviour** field is under **Configuration → Campaign Settings**.
  - The options are **Restart on republish**, **Count delay only while published**, and **Count delay regardless of publish state**.
  - **Count delay regardless of publish state** is the global default.
  - **Use global setting** appears only on the Campaign create and edit form. New Campaigns have it selected by default.
- The setting affects only events with relative (interval) delays. It doesn't change events with absolute dates.
- All three examples are correct (Jan 11, Jan 17, Jan 16). The calculation matches `EventScheduler::extendTriggerDateWhenCampaignUnpublished()`.
- The new Cron note is correct. Mautic recalculates a pending event only after its original date arrives and the Campaign is active. If the new date is in the past, the event runs in that Cron run. If the new date is in the future, Mautic reschedules the event.
- If a Campaign uses **Use global setting**, the activation message shows the global option. The message text in the PR matches the UI exactly.
- The Contact History fix is correct. The **Campaign event scheduled** entry reads 'Scheduled to execute at {date}' and shows no reason, even after a reschedule. Removing the old claim was right.
- Vale reports nothing new in the changed lines. The one error and the warnings in these four files are also on the `7.2` base.

### What to fix
1. **Line 60, from your review comment.** Remove the explanation of why the labels differ, and tell readers what they'll see instead. Suggested text:
   ```rst
   In the UI, this setting appears as **Campaign Republish Behaviour**. You can set it in two places:
   ```
   The two places aren't sequential steps, so use `*` bullets instead of `#.`.
2. **"Activate and deactivate Campaigns" is too narrow.** The activation message appears in two places: the Campaigns list, and the **Active** toggle on an existing Campaign's edit form. It doesn't appear when you create a Campaign. Turning a Campaign off also shows a confirmation. The old text mentioned this confirmation, but the PR removed it. Suggested text:
   ```rst
   When you turn on an existing Campaign, either from the Campaigns list or with the **Active** toggle when editing the Campaign, Mautic displays a confirmation message that shows the republish behavior in effect. If the Campaign uses **Use global setting**, the message shows the global option.

   When you turn off a Campaign, Mautic asks you to confirm that you want to stop processing Contacts and Campaign events, including scheduled events.
   ```
3. **Quote style.** The PR puts the confirmation message in double quotes. The style guide uses single quotes for text that Mautic displays, as the earlier version did: 'All scheduled events will execute according to the Republish Behavior setting. Currently set to: Count delay regardless of publish state.'
4. **"Event scheduled: January 1" is ambiguous.** Readers can take it as the date the event runs. The calculation actually starts on the date the Contact reached the event. Use `* Contact reaches the event: January 1` in all three examples.
5. **The restart option has two different labels.** The new note uses **Allow contacts to restart the campaign**, which is the exact UI text. The Creating Campaigns page uses **Allow Contacts to restart the Campaign**. Use the same form on both pages.

### Missing details to add
1. **Scheduled activation works the same way.** Mautic treats the scheduled activation and deactivation dates (Publish Up and Publish Down) the same as turning the Campaign on and off by hand:
   - **Count delay only while published** doesn't count time before a scheduled activation date or after a scheduled deactivation date.
   - **Restart on republish** starts the delay again from the scheduled activation date.

   I confirmed both in the running app. Add a sentence near the top of the section. Then link to it from the **Active** bullet on the Creating Campaigns page ("You can also schedule to activate or deactivate a Campaign at a future date…").
2. **What the Campaign details panel shows.** The panel has two related rows:
   - **Campaign Republish Behaviour** shows the text **Use global setting** when the Campaign follows the global default, not the option in effect. The confirmation message is different: it shows the option in effect.
   - **Last Publish Date** shows the scheduled activation date if the Campaign became active that way. It shows 'N/A' only if the Campaign was never active.

   Suggested text for "Viewing last activation date":
   ```rst
   The Campaign details panel shows two related values:

   * **Campaign Republish Behaviour** - the option set for this Campaign. If the Campaign follows the global default, this shows **Use global setting**.
   * **Last Publish Date** - the date the Campaign most recently became active, either when you turned it on or on its scheduled activation date. **Restart on republish** counts the delay from this date.
   ```
3. **Optional, for "Tracking rescheduled events":** You can reschedule or cancel the event by hand from the same Contact History entry. After you cancel an event, you can't reschedule it. One sentence or a link would help admins who come to this page to troubleshoot.

I checked the confirmation messages in the page HTML of the running 7.2 instance, on the list toggle, the edit-form toggle, and the new Campaign form. I didn't click through the pop-ups in a browser.

Thanks @adiati98! I’ve addressed the Promptless suggestions and removed the explanation about the differing labels. I’ve also personally reviewed the revised documentation before pushing this update.

Since mautic/mautic#17678 has now merged into 7.2, this revision uses the updated reactivation terminology throughout and refreshes the activation confirmation screenshot. It also clarifies scheduled activation and deactivation, the Campaign Details rows, confirmations when editing an existing Campaign, and when the Cron job recalculates delays. The related pages link to the central section.

I checked the UI in a local Mautic 7.2.1 instance with the merged Campaign translations applied and verified the scheduling behavior with controlled test Contacts. The docs build succeeds with no new warnings, Vale has no new findings compared with the unchanged baseline, and the link check reports no broken links.

@promptless-for-oss this PR is updated following the code fix made at https://github.com/mautic/mautic/pull/17678. Investigate the current codebase and review this PR. Follow our style guides.

Post your findings and a summary as a comment on the PR. Don't commit any changes, push to the branch, or open a new PR.

Thanks, @adiati98. I'm reviewing this PR against the current Mautic code, including the fix in mautic/mautic#17678, and against the Mautic style guides, and I'll post my findings and a summary here without changing the branch.

@adiati98, here's my review of the updated PR, with a summary first. Thanks to mahmudurrahmanlabib for the revisions. I checked head `075f9b9` against the `mautic/mautic` 7.2 source at `522d2c7`, which includes the merged fix from mautic/mautic#17678 (`78108ca`). I didn't commit, push or open a PR.

**Summary:** The PR now matches the current code. It uses the new reactivation labels, and it addresses every item from my previous review. I found no accuracy problems. Five small items are left, all about style and wording.

### Confirmed against the current code
- **Labels.** These match `CampaignBundle/Translations/en_US/messages.ini` after #17678:
  - **Campaign Reactivation Behaviour**
  - **Restart on reactivation**, **Count delay only while active** and **Count delay regardless of activation state**
  - **Use global setting**
  - **Last Activation Date**
  - The activation message: 'All scheduled events will execute according to the Reactivation Behaviour setting. Currently set to: …'

  Using UK "Behaviour" in the bold UI labels and US "behavior" in the prose and headings is correct.
- **Default.** **Count delay regardless of activation state** is the global default (`EventScheduler.php:185`).
- **Use global setting.** This option appears only on the Campaign form (`CampaignType`, `include_global_option`). When a Campaign inherits the default, the Details panel shows **Use global setting** (`details.html.twig:92`).
- **Examples.** The three example dates are correct (January 11, January 17 and January 16). They match `EventScheduler::extendTriggerDateWhenCampaignUnpublished()`.
- **Scheduled activation and deactivation.** `PublishStateService` splits active periods at the scheduled activation and deactivation dates. The **Last Activation Date** is the scheduled activation date when one applies. Line 57 and the line 153 bullet are both accurate.
- **Confirmation messages.** The activation message shows the option in effect, including the global option when the Campaign inherits it. It appears on the Campaigns list toggle (`PublishToggleSubscriber`) and on the **Active** toggle when you edit an existing Campaign. It doesn't appear when you create a Campaign (`CampaignType.php:72`, which checks `getId()`). Turning a Campaign off asks for confirmation in both places. Lines 160–168 are accurate.
- **Cron note (line 176) and the January 11 result (line 99).** The Cron job only picks up a pending event when its date has arrived and the Campaign is active (`LeadEventLogRepository::getScheduled()`). At that point it recalculates the date. It reschedules the event if the new date is in the future and runs it if the date has passed (`ScheduledExecutioner::validateSchedule()`).
- **Contact History.** The entry label **Campaign event scheduled** matches the UI, and the `:ref:` to `History` resolves.
- **Screenshot.** The new screenshot shows the exact post-#17678 activation message.
- **Build and Vale.** A full Sphinx HTML build reports nothing new for these pages; the four warnings on these pages come from lines this PR doesn't change. Vale reports the same 44 findings on the `7.2` base and on this branch, and none are on changed lines.

### Small fixes
1. **`managing_campaigns.rst` line 62.** The "In the UI, this setting appears as" wording came from my last review. It was useful when the UI said "Republish" and the docs said "reactivation". Now that they match, the sentence explains a label readers will already recognize. Suggested text:
   ```rst
   You can set **Campaign Reactivation Behaviour** in two places:
   ```
2. **`managing_campaigns.rst` line 44.** The new label `.. _Campaign republish behavior:` uses the retired term, and nothing refers to it. All four `:ref:` links point to the `Campaign reactivation behavior` heading. Remove the label, unless you're keeping it on purpose so old `#campaign-republish-behavior` links keep working.
3. **`managing_campaigns.rst` line 148.** The Details panel opens and closes in place; it isn't a menu. The page also spells it "drop-down" at line 20 and "dropdown" here. Suggested text:
   ```rst
   On the Campaign's page, expand **Details** to view these settings:
   ```
   I'd also add to the **Last Activation Date** bullet: "If the Campaign has never been active, this row shows 'N/A'."
4. **Heading style in the section.** The PR changed "Configuring" to **Configure reactivation behavior**, but its siblings still use the "-ing" form: **Viewing reactivation details** and **Tracking rescheduled events**. Pick one form for all of them, for example "Configuring reactivation behavior" to match the existing headings.
5. **`importing_campaigns.rst` line 97.** The blank line after the warning text has trailing spaces. Remove them.

### Optional
- **Line 85.** "Mautic uses the original trigger date" mixes in a different term now that the examples say "Contact reaches the event". Suggested text: "Mautic keeps the originally calculated event date, and inactive time doesn't affect scheduling."
- **Line 57.** This paragraph mentions **Count delay only while active** and **Restart on reactivation** before the page introduces them. It might read better at the end of **Reactivation behavior options**.

I checked this round against the source code, the Sphinx build and Vale. I didn't click through the confirmation pop-ups in a running instance this time; the January 11/17/16 example results were tested in a running Mautic 7.2 instance during the previous review.

Test now actually asserts the filter narrows results. Good.

rawCodeReviews.body: I see no other issues. Thanks Fedy! 👍

Verified Below scenarios, working as expected.
### 1. Email Preview Download Page Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | Admin can access download preview page | Navigate to `/email/download/preview/{emailId}` as admin | Page loads with top bar, contact/company lookups, iframe, and "Download HTML" button |
| 1.2 | Anonymous user blocked from unpublished email | Open `/email/download/preview/{emailId}` in incognito for unpublished email | HTTP 403 Forbidden |
| 1.3 | Anonymous user can access published email with public preview | Open `/email/download/preview/{emailId}` in incognito for published email with public preview enabled | Page loads successfully |
| 1.4 | Non-admin with viewown can access own emails | Login as non-admin with `email:emails:viewown`, access own email preview | Page loads successfully |
| 1.5 | Non-admin blocked from other users' emails | Login as non-admin with `email:emails:viewown`, try to access another user's email | HTTP 403 Forbidden |

### 2. Contact Token Rendering Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | Preview with contact shows real token values | Select a contact in the preview, email has `{contactfield=firstname}` | Contact's actual first name appears in preview |
| 2.2 | Preview without contact shows placeholder tokens | View preview without selecting contact | `[Firstname]` placeholder appears |
| 2.3 | Contact lookup updates preview dynamically | Change selected contact in lookup field | Preview iframe reloads with new contact's data |
| 2.4 | Clearing contact reverts to placeholders | Select contact, then clear the lookup field | Preview shows placeholder tokens again |

### 3. Company Token Rendering Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | Preview with company shows real token values | Select a company, email has `{companyfield=companyname}` | Company's actual name appears in preview |
| 3.2 | Preview without company shows placeholder tokens | View preview without selecting company | `[Companyname]` placeholder appears |
| 3.3 | Company lookup updates preview dynamically | Change selected company in lookup field | Preview iframe reloads with new company's data |
| 3.4 | Contact's primary company used when no company selected | Select contact with companies, don't select company manually | Contact's primary company tokens rendered |

### 4. Permission Enforcement Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | Non-admin cannot view contact they don't own | Login as non-admin with `viewown`, select contact owned by another user | Error flash: "You do not have access to this contact", tokens render as placeholders |
| 4.2 | Non-admin can view contact they own | Login as non-admin with `viewown`, select contact they own | Contact's real token values appear, no error |
| 4.3 | Admin can view any contact | Login as admin, select any contact | Contact's real token values appear |
| 4.4 | User with viewother can view any contact | Login with `lead:leads:viewother`, select any contact | Contact's real token values appear |

### 5. HTML Download Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1 | Download HTML without contact/company | Click "Download HTML" with no contact/company selected | File downloads as `email-name.html` with placeholder tokens |
| 5.2 | Download HTML with contact | Select contact "John", click "Download HTML" | File downloads as `john-email-name.html` |
| 5.3 | Download HTML with company | Select company "Acme Corp", click "Download HTML" | File downloads as `acme-corp-email-name.html` |
| 5.4 | Download HTML with both | Select contact and company, download | Company name takes precedence in filename |
| 5.5 | Downloaded HTML contains rendered tokens | Download with contact selected | HTML file contains actual contact data, not tokens |
| 5.6 | Special characters sanitized in filename | Contact name is "O'Neill", download | Filename is `o-neill-email-name.html` |

### 6. Company Lookup AJAX Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6.1 | Admin sees all companies | As admin, type in company lookup | All matching companies appear |
| 6.2 | Non-admin with viewown sees only owned companies | As non-admin with `viewown`, type in company lookup | Only companies they own appear |
| 6.3 | Company lookup returns correct format | Make AJAX call to `lead:companyList` | Returns `{id, value}` pairs with `success: 1` |

### 7. Draft Preview Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7.1 | Draft preview URL updates with contact/company | Select contact/company on email with draft | Draft preview URL includes `contactId` and `companyId` parameters |
| 7.2 | Draft preview shows draft content with tokens | Access draft preview with contact | Draft content displayed with contact's token values |
| 7.3 | Draft public preview requires published status | Access draft preview anonymously for unpublished email with public draft preview | Access denied |

### 8. Email Detail Page Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8.1 | Company lookup field visible | Open email detail page | Company lookup field appears alongside contact lookup |
| 8.2 | Preview URL updates with both IDs | Select contact and company | Preview URL contains both `contactId` and `companyId` params |
| 8.3 | Preview iframe updates on selection | Select contact or company | Iframe reloads with updated token values |
| 8.4 | Hidden input for company ID exists | Inspect page | `#content_preview_settings_company_id` hidden input present |

### 9. Token Regex Tests

| # | Test Case | Steps | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
